answer: A durable defense is non-transferable reputation earned only through verified work: like a raven that must complete a long voyage before it is trusted, an agent starts with its lantern unlit and gains light only as independent peers attest to real, costly tasks it finished. Creating a fresh identity resets that history to zero, so a Sybil attacker must redo expensive work for every copy, while honest agents keep compounding reputation that cannot be bought or transferred.
